distanthorizons.config.client.advanced.g:
How far can ye see before the fog gets ye.

We're trying our best captain, but we may veer a bit off course.
How far before the luster of the distant land becomes less like gold and more like wood.
The shiniest the far shores can be
How well yer distant lands can show yer ship's sails and gun-deck.

Do ye want to look from yer eye or from yer hat.
If yer hat is away from its perch ye could see fartharrr.

(Especially when magic portals can steal yer hat).
If ye got this yer spyglass is clean, if not ye got a blurry glass!
When use'n yer spyglass, how much more luster can we see?
How long yer distant lands can travel before loosing their luster.
How ye distant lands should be colored.
How yer distant lands should be colored
When looking at land, how should the greenery look?

If true nearby LODs will render blocks with their real shape 
instead of full cubes. 
If false all LODs render as full cubes. 

Only applies to the highest detail LODs.
Smooths out the distant lands, else ye be sailing and see a sharp end of the world.
How should the unflavored terrain fade when lookin at it?
Fade Before End Of The World
Should yer vision fade before we reach the edge of the world?
The higher ye go the smoother yer lands and waters'll be.
Adds shadows to the corners of yer ship.
Ironin' yer Sails stills the shimmerin' horizon whilst on the move.
If allowed ye'll see the weather and the lights from far off ports.
See Lights From Far Off Ports
How far up those distant lights go. Requires a ship reload t' take effect.
If aye, distant lights get larger the further ye be. If nay, they stay 1 block wide.
If aye, distant lights to be seen.
If allowed ye can tell the weather.
A list of all the lands we can see the weather in.

Nay = One layer o'clouds for the cap'n, just like on the high seas.
Aye = 3 layers o'clouds for the cap'n, if ye like the thick weather.
Do we put fog on the distant lands?
Where we get our fog's color.

§6Aye:§r Minecraft renders fog like normal.
§6False:§r disables Minecraft's fog on vanilla chunks.

Where should th' fog begin?

  '0.0': Fog begins at yer ship's wheel.
  '1.0': Th' fog-start's circle fits exactly in th' LOD render distance square.
'1.414': Th' LOD render distance square fits exactly in th' fog-start's circle.

Where should th' fog end? 

  '0.0': Fog ends at yer ship's wheel.
  '1.0': Th' fog-end's circle fits exactly in th' LOD render distance square.
'1.414': Th' LOD render distance square fits exactly in th' fog-end's circle.

What be th' minimum fog thickness? 

  '0.0': Nary a fog.
  '1.0': Completely fog colored.

What be th' minimum fog thickness? 

  '0.0': Nary a fog.
  '1.0': Completely fog colored.

How should th' fog thickness be calculated? 

LINEAR: Linear based on distance (will ignore 'density')
EXPONENTIAL: 1/(e^(distance*density)) 
EXPONENTIAL_SQUARED: 1/(e^((distance*density)^2))
What be th' sea smoke's density?

Defines how height affects th' fog. 
When in doubt start with SPHERICAL, ADDITION, or MAX. 

SPHERICAL: Fog is calculated based on spyglass distance. 
CYLINDRICAL: Ignore height, fog is calculated based on horizontal distance. 
MAX: max(heightFog, farFog) 
ADDITION: heightFog + farFog 
MULTIPLY: heightFog * farFog 
INVERSE_MULTIPLY: 1 - (1-heightFog) * (1-farFog) 
LIMITED_ADDITION: farFog + max(farFog, heightFog) 
MULTIPLY_ADDITION: farFog + farFog * heightFog 
INVERSE_MULTIPLY_ADDITION: farFog + 1 - (1-heightFog) * (1-farFog) 
AVERAGE: farFog*0.5 + heightFog*0.5

Where should th' height fog be located? 

ABOVE_CAMERA: Height fog starts from th' spyglass to th' sky 
BELOW_CAMERA: Height fog starts from th' spyglass to Davy Jones' locker 
ABOVE_AND_BELOW_CAMERA: Height fog starts from th' spyglass to both th' sky and th' locker 
ABOVE_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog starts from a set height to th' sky 
BELOW_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog starts from a set height to th' locker 
ABOVE_AND_BELOW_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog starts from a set height to both th' sky and th' locker
If th' height fog be calculated around a set height, what be that height position?

How far th' start of height fog should offset? 

  '0.0': Fog starts wit' no offset.
  '1.0': Fog starts wit' offset of th' entire sea's height. (Include depth)

How far th' end of height fog should offset? 

  '0.0': Fog ends wit' no offset.
  '1.0': Fog ends wit' offset of th' entire sea's height. (Include depth)

What be th' minimum fog thickness? 

  '0.0': Nary a fog.
  '1.0': Completely fog colored.

What be th' minimum fog thickness? 

  '0.0': Nary a fog.
  '1.0': Completely fog colored.

How should th' height fog thickness be calculated? 

LINEAR: Linear based on height (will ignore 'density')
EXPONENTIAL: 1/(e^(height*density)) 
EXPONENTIAL_SQUARED: 1/(e^((height*density)^2))
What be th' height fog's density?

If aye, nearby and zoomed-in LODs will render wit' their block's 
actual picture and silhouette instead of a single flat color. 

Only applies to high detail LODs where th' picture be actually visible, 
distant LODs always use flat colors. 
Has no effect while a shader pack be active, since shader packs 
render LODs wit' their own spells.

Th' highest detail level number that can render wit' block pictures. 
At higher detail levels each LOD covers multiple blocks, 
makin' pictures smaller than a pixel and therefore invisible. 

Larger numbers picture more distant LODs 
but take up more thinkin'.

A comma separated list of block resource locations
 that DH won't render pictures on.
 Partial matches/incomplete resource locations will also match.

 Example: "minecraft:grass_block,nylium"

 Changes require ye t' dock and reload yer game.

A comma separated list of block resource locations\n that DH will render their sides usin' th' bottom picture. 
Partial matches/incomplete resource locations will also match. 

Example: "minecraft:grass_block,nylium" 

Changes require ye t' dock and reload yer game.
Block Tags Don't Use Side Picture

A comma separated list of tag names
 that DH will render their sides usin' th' bottom picture. 

Example: "grass_blocks,nylium" 

Changes require ye t' dock and reload yer game.

A comma separated list of block resource locations 
that DH will use rasterization to determine 
th' face pictures.

Can be used t' fix issues wit' mods/blocks where 
a side uses just part of a modeled block's picture. 

Example: "minecraft:beacon" 

Changes require ye t' dock and reload yer game.
If aye, a grit picture will be applied to LODs to simulate pictures.
Sets how much grit are on the distant lands.

How far the grit should go before it cleans up (in blocks). 
Set to 0 to disable grit from fading away.

How far from yer eyes can the distant lands appear. 
-1 = Auto, changes based on yer spyglass.

Higher values will prevent LODs from rendering behind vanilla blocks at a higher distance,
but may cause holes to appear in the LODs. 
Holes are most likely to appear when flying through unloaded terrain. 

Increasing the vanilla render distance increases the effectiveness of this setting.
If ye be sailing quickly ye'll become near sighted. But ye won't see gaps in the map.

If allowed ye'll be unable t' see caves. 

Extra Info: Hides faces with skylight value of 0 under the cave hiding height
How far up should we hide the caves?
If allowed yer far lights will be hidden so ye won't see em up close.
Pretends ye have eyes on the back of yer head. Distant lands will be shown even when ye aint looking.
Pretends ye have eyes on the back of yer head when moving a candle through yer ship.
We don't be caring 'bout these here bits o land.
A list of blocks in caves we don't care nothing about.
Blocks to hide under the waves
A list of blocks we should put under the waves.
A list of blocks we don't want to see on our open seas.

Defines what blocks should be rendered as LODs. 

§6NONE:§r Include all blocks in the LODs
§6NON_COLLIDING:§r Only render solid blocks in the LODs (tall grass, torches, etc. will be ignored)
Can make yer captain's carpet look bad

distanthorizons.config.client.advanced.d:
If aye, this will disable (most) standard Minecraft doodlin'. 

NOTE: Do nah report any foul seas when this mode be on!

Mod compatibility be nah guaranteed.

F6 - enable/disable LOD doodlin' 
F7 - enable/disable LOD only doodlin' 
F8 - cycle through th' different de-buggin' doodlin' modes

If aye, vertex color will nah be passed.
Useful for de-buggin' shaders.

If aye, overlapping quads will be drawn as bright red fer easy identification. 
If nay, th' quads will be drawn normally.

distanthorizons.config.common.worldGener: Missing World
Allow filling in missing worlds
If allowed we'll fill in the holes around yer map as ye play.
Lookout Trainin' Funds

Defines how LODs will be generated 
outside the vanilla render distance 
in singleplayer. 

Some options may be unavailable depending on MC version. 

§6SURFACE_THEN_CHUNKS§r 
Recommended for modded or vanilla worlds. 

§6SURFACE_ONLY§r 
Recommended for computers that don't have 
enough CPU power or RAM space to handle 
chunk generation. 

§6CHUNKS_ONLY§r 
Recommended for custom worlds 
where the surface generator would 
generate incorrect terrain. 

§6DISABLED§r
Recommended if you experience lag.
Quadrant Chartin' Way
How many lads be keepin' eyes on lookout when spyin' distant shores.
Swiften The Seas

Restart yer world afore these new orders take hold.

If set t' aye, Distant Horizons will chart a rough
lay o' the land afore ye can shout “Land ho!”,
fillin' the view clear out t' yer render distance.

Once that rough chart be drawn, Distant Horizons
will forge each chunk, followin' the orders
in yer "distantGeneratorMode" settin', bringin'
trees an' structures into view.

If ye sail a wholly custom world,
best set this option t' nay, matey,
lest ordinary terrain come creepin' over yer horizon.
See missing world voyage
How our voyage to fill in yer map should be shown.
How often to update yer voyage
How often should we tell you about our voyage.
See extra instructions for this long
How long should the first mate give ye extra instructions. He'll take em away afterwards.
See Missing World Speed
Should the first mate include the speed for our missing world voyage?
Hold fire if the Hull be Crackin'

If this 'ere ship ain't be threadin' swift enough
The seas shall freeze in their booties for reducin' shudders.
Hold when Sail in Wind

If yer ship be ahead of the wind
yer maps will keep their secrets but yer voyage will be
smooth sailin'.
How many Hands repairing Deck
'Tis the percentage o' the full LOD spyglass horizon that the second wave o' the speedy surface scallywag will pack wi' chunks conjured up just like yer "distantGeneratorMode" decrees.
distanthorizons.config.common.lodBuildin: Ignore lands we've seen before, only look to new lands.
How should we put yer clothes in the locker?
Can we put everything in yer locker? Or will ye care if we toss a few of these here trinkets?

Loosenin' these rules speeds up yer database's read/write
work, but risks sendin' yer data overboard or corruptin' it if
yer computer's power gives out.
(Should the program abandon ship unexpectedly,
all options should keep yer cargo safe.)

§6FULL§r
ACID - yer data shall never be lost at sea or corrupted
Slow as a barnacled ship

§6NORMAL§r
Some data may go overboard if the power gives out,
but yer database shouldn't be corrupted.
Swift sailin'

§6OFF§r
Yer database may be corrupted if the power gives out
Swifter sailin' still
Fill distant lands with rough maps
When allowed yer distant lands can be filled in with large rough maps.
distanthorizons.config.common.multiThrea: How many threads DH will use.

What Java thread priority should DH's primary thread pools run with?

Ye probably don't need t' change this unless ye are also 
runnin' C2ME and are seein' thread starvation in either C2ME or DH.

If C2ME be present, set DH's thread count t' match C2ME. 

This be necessary t' prevent thread starvation issues when C2ME be present.
distanthorizons.config.common.logging.@t: Controls how loggin' should be handled.
distanthorizons.config.common.logging.wa: Show Low Memory Warnin' On Startup
If DH detects that pooled objects are bein' garbage collected this will send a chat warnin'.
Show High Standard Render Distance Warnin'
distanthorizons.config.server.sendLevelK:
Makes th' island send level keys fer each sea.
Disable this if ye use alternative ways t' send level keys.
distanthorizons.config.server.levelKeyPr:
Prefix of th' level keys sent to th' ships.
If th' mod be runnin' behind a proxy, each backend should use a unique value.
If this value be empty, level key will be based on th' island's seed hash.
distanthorizons.config.server.generation:
How many LOD generation requests per second should a ship send?
Also limits th' number of ship requests allowed t' stay in th' island's queue.
distanthorizons.config.server.maxGenerat: Defines th' distance allowed t' generate around th' sailor.
distanthorizons.config.server.enableReal: If aye, ships will receive real-time LOD updates fer chunks outside th' ship's render distance.
distanthorizons.config.server.realTimeUp: Defines th' distance th' sailor will receive updates around.
distanthorizons.config.server.synchroniz: If aye, ships will receive updated LODs when joinin' or loadin' new LODs.
distanthorizons.config.server.syncOnLoad: Rate Limit fer Sync on Load

How many LOD sync requests per second should a ship send?
Also limits th' number of ship's requests allowed t' stay in th' island's queue.
distanthorizons.config.server.maxSyncOnL: Max Sync on Load Request Distance

Defines th' distance allowed t' be synchronized around th' sailor.
Should be th' same or larger than maxGenerationRequestDistance in most cases.
distanthorizons.config.server.playerBand:
Maximum per-sailor speed fer uploadin' LODs t' th' ships, in KB/s.
Value of 0 disables th' limit.
distanthorizons.config.server.globalBand:
Maximum global speed fer uploadin' LODs t' th' ships, in KB/s.
Value of 0 disables th' limit.
distanthorizons.config.server.enableAdap:
"Enables adaptive transfer speed based on ship performance.
If aye, DH will automatically adjust transfer rate t' minimize connection lag.
If nay, transfer speed will remain fixed.
